evals.prompt: Our forecast is always wrong. Should we buy an AI forecasting tool?
evals.expected_output: Should say no: a tool trained on optimistic data produces confident optimistic forecasts. Should fix stage definitions first, tying them to buyer actions rather than seller activities, and apply the rule that a deal with no next meeting scheduled is not in the pipeline. Should recommend tracking slip rate and publishing forecast-to-actual delta.
assertions: Explains a tool on bad data produces confident bad output
Requires stage definitions tied to buyer actions
Recommends measuring forecast accuracy over time

evals.prompt: We have 5 customers. Should we design a commission plan and set quotas?
evals.expected_output: Should say this is premature: rev ops turns a documented playbook into a system, and there is no playbook yet at 5 customers. Should recommend the founder run the first 5-10 deals and document. Should still give the comp principles for later: simple enough to compute mentally, pay for what you want more of, uncapped at the top.
assertions: States this is premature at 5 customers
Explains rev ops systematizes an existing playbook
Recommends the founder run and document the first deals
Gives comp principles for when the time comes
Notes paying on bookings gets bookings including churned ones
